draft.title: Rutherford's nuclear model
card: In the Geiger-Marsden experiment, alpha particles (positive particles) were fired at a very thin gold foil. A detector screen showed where they ended up.
Most alpha particles went straight through, or bent only slightly. So most of an atom is empty space.
A very small number were deflected through large angles, and a few bounced almost straight back. Only a strong force from a concentrated positive charge could do this.
Rutherford concluded that an atom has a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus, which holds nearly all of its mass. The electrons lie outside it.
draft.remember: Most alpha particles passed through, a few bounced back: the atom has a tiny, dense, positive nucleus.

a.q: What did the few alpha particles that bounced almost straight back show about the gold atoms?
opts: Each atom has a tiny, dense, positive centre
Each atom is a uniform ball of positive charge
Each atom has electrons spread through its whole volume
Each atom is mostly made of negative charge
a.why: A large deflection needs a strong repulsion from a small region holding concentrated positive charge and mass. A uniform ball of positive charge would only bend alpha particles slightly, so that option is tempting but wrong.
a.clue: Only a concentrated charge could turn a fast particle right around.

b.q: In a repeat of the experiment, a student sees that almost all alpha particles pass straight through the foil. What does this observation show?
opts: Most of the atom is empty space
The nucleus takes up most of the atom's volume
Alpha particles are not affected by positive charge
The gold atoms have no electrons
b.why: If almost all particles pass undeflected, then most of the atom's volume has no concentrated charge or mass in the way. The nucleus is tiny, so the second option is the reverse of what is seen. The few large deflections, not the passing through, are what show the nucleus is positive.
b.clue: What must most of the atom be like if particles are not turned aside?

a.best: Each atom has a tiny, dense, positive centre

b.best: Most of the atom is empty space

problems.detail: Why (b) calls the wrong answer about the nucleus 'the second option'. The options are shuffled, and in this order the second option is 'Alpha particles are not affected by positive charge', not 'The nucleus takes up most of the atom's volume'. The why should name the option by its text, not its position.

check.summary: The physics is correct and both questions have one clear right answer. The only problem is that why (b) points to a wrong answer as 'the second option', which will name the wrong option once the options are shuffled.
